close_reason: Already fixed before this session: anchor NC state is seeded before the chain walk loop at lines 1267-1298. The anchor_nc integration tests (valid_leaf_passes_permitted_nc, leaf_violating_permitted_fails, leaf_in_excluded_subtree_fails) all pass, demonstrating anchor NC constraints are enforced correctly.
description: chain_walk seeds nc_permitted/nc_excluded as empty, then calls check_name_constraints before updating state. For the first cert in the walk (i = chain.len()-1, the root-adjacent cert), NC state is always empty so its names are never checked against anchor-supplied initial_permitted/initial_excluded from RFC 5280 §6.1.1(b). RFC 5280 §6.1.1 requires the initial-permitted and initial-excluded subtrees to be initialized from the trust anchor configuration, not left empty. No anchor-sourced NC constraints ever take effect — a misconfigured anchor that should restrict names admits all names silently. Trigger: caller installs a trust anchor with a name constraint (e.g., requiring DNS names under .example.com); any cert chain passes regardless.
title: NC check called on anchor-issued cert before NC state is seeded from anchor
